scope: Saved-frame analysis of two completed 20 ns CPD runs and the first 20 ns of three archived unmodified 2hb_1xT production jobs.
conclusion: Both CPD cores meet a provisional numerical/structural MVP interpretation over the observed 20 ns. Global motion is comparable to the approximate baselines. Cis-anti-I has an unresolved late flanking base-pair opening; cis-syn-I has an earlier transient local opening that recovers. Neither result establishes force-field accuracy or equilibrium.

excluded_baseline.reason: Job metadata says completed 200 ns, but currently retained DCD has only 1226 frames spanning 69.81–82.06 ns; cannot compare its first 20 ns.

method.local_region: Two extra thymine nucleotides plus the immediately preceding and following residues on their strands; D001 residues 14–16 and D000 residues 7–9.
method.pairing_criterion: Every canonical donor/acceptor heavy-atom distance in a pair <= the common initial-design reference distance + 0.75 A; minimum-image distances. Not an angular H-bond criterion.
method.rmsd: Each group independently rigid-aligned to its own production-job start; same DNA sequence and atom identities verified.
method.periodic_images: Stored unwrapped DNA coordinates for modern runs; fragment unwrapping and assembly image reconstruction for older wrapAll-on baseline.
method.cpd_reference_distances: The two CPD reference plans have identical pair identities and reference distances; those same thresholds were mapped by atom identity to all baselines.
method.plot: Nonoverlapping 1 ns means; complete sampled-frame traces retained in CSV.

chemistry: Both intended crosslinks exist in PSF; all seven packaged assets hash-verified for each CPD run; four stereocenters retain expected signed volumes in every saved frame. Crosslink lengths average approximately 1.55–1.56 A. No coordinate nonfiniteness or pathological lesion/DNA heavy-atom close contacts found (minimum nonbonded distance 2.44 A, excluding 1–2 and 1–3 neighbors).
protocol_differences: CPDs: 2 fs, ordinary masses, roughly 472624 atoms, approximately 141 x 163 x 208 A box.
Newer baselines: 4 fs/HMR, 62677 atoms, approximately 60 x 83 x 130 A box. Shared relaxation parent, different production seeds.
Older baseline: 4 fs/HMR, 21436 atoms, approximately 44 x 67 x 114 A box; Langevin damping 5 rather than 1; starts after a prior 2 ns production job.
Starting geometries and relaxation histories differ. These are useful empirical baselines, not matched causal controls.
interpretation: Whole-DNA RMSD growth and terminal fraying are also seen in the baselines; the CPD trajectories are not exceptional on those measures.
The crosslinked six-residue regions move less than the newer unlinked baselines; a covalent linkage itself restricts motion, so lower RMSD alone does not validate the force field.
Cis-syn-I local pairing falls around 5–10 ns then recovers to baseline-like occupancy in the final 5 ns.

Cis-anti-I D000:THY9–D002:ADE9 pairing drops late: approximately 40% occupancy in the last 5 ns versus 90–97% in the three baselines. This is a local difference worth reproducing, not proof of an incorrect force field.
next_decision: Keep both as provisional MVP elements. Do not retune parameters solely to suppress observed opening. Prioritize a cis-anti-I repeat and a matched non-CPD baseline with the same box/integrator/relaxation protocol if deciding whether local destabilization is lesion-specific.
limitations: One current CPD trajectory per isomer; saved frames are correlated and are not independent replicas.
No inference about unsaved 2 fs transients; sample spacing is 20 ps for CPDs.
Fixed product topology cannot validate photochemical formation, bond-breaking kinetics, or isomer free energies.
No equilibrium or broad origami transferability certification; no simulation settings changed.
